examples.title: A progress panel that does not own the loop
examples.brief: A fictional terminal app needs visible streaming progress.
examples.before: Copy the orchestrator into the UI and add a custom session store.
examples.after: Read the installed hook/event contract; subscribe in the client, retain Core execution custody, and test cleanup on cancellation.
examples.why: Composition and lifecycle ownership keep UI interaction separate from the execution engine.

marketing.headline: Add the capability. Keep the architecture clear.
marketing.lead: A working guide for people extending Amplifier. Find the right home for a feature, build one useful slice, and check that it behaves correctly inside the host you actually use.

benefits.title: Choose the right seam
benefits.body: Separate application interaction, reusable bundle wiring, callable tools, hooks and providers before adding code.

benefits.title: Keep the useful context
benefits.body: Six substantial reference topics cover Core, Foundation, module authoring, application integration, routing and work across repositories.

benefits.title: Hand over a working slice
benefits.body: Make inputs, errors, cancellation and cleanup explicit, with commands someone else can repeat.

walkthrough.title: Inspect the host
walkthrough.detail: Read its manifests, installed contracts and a neighboring implementation. Record what version the advice applies to.

walkthrough.title: Build the smallest slice
walkthrough.detail: Agree the observable behavior and ownership, then implement through the seam that already owns it.

walkthrough.title: Prove and hand over
walkthrough.detail: Check registration, success, invalid input, cancellation and cleanup; record installation and rollback.

use_when: You need to add a tool, hook, provider or bundle.
A client feature is starting to duplicate the execution engine.
A change spans Core, Foundation and an application.
not_for: A replacement Amplifier runtime or a new provider configuration.
Blindly copying historical API signatures into a different installed version.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Build with Amplifier to inspect this repository. I want a progress panel for a long-running tool. Decide where the feature belongs, identify the actual event contract, and propose one slice with cancellation and cleanup checks.
marketing.output_preview:
Fictional slice: import progress
UI owns: display and user cancellation
Core owns: tool execution
Contract: current host event schema, inspected revision recorded
Checks: success, error, cancel, listener cleanup
Open evidence: real-host run pending
marketing.proof_summary: The six-topic reference mirror, isolated helper regressions and complete portable installation are checked. These checks establish retained content and software behavior; a new extension still needs validation in its actual host.
marketing.next_step: Bring one feature request and the repository where it should work.
marketing.example_note: Fictional worked example. It illustrates the intended output; it is not a measured result or a real customer story.
install_notes: Requires Git and Python 3.11+ for the repository installer. The portable method itself can be read by a compatible agent without a service or provider account.
The destination is a skills-parent folder. Use the discovery path supported by your agent; ~/.agents/skills is an example, not a universal host setting.
Keep the complete installed folder, references and license together. Identical reinstall is safe; conflicts are refused. A deliberate --replace keeps a dated backup.

portable.output: Build the extension in the right place, against the current contracts.
portable.failure: Report insufficient evidence, unsupported context or host limitation; never turn discovery into an execution claim.

native.status: Existing declared entrypoints preserved; runtime signatures, service access and installation tests remain separate evidence.

installation.scope: Shared canonical portable installer only; not the legacy repository helper or native package installation.

secret_names.native_runtime_inventory: See native documentation; no credentials are bundled or inferred.

dataflow.installation: Shared canonical portable installer only (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/): read portable source tracked at the explicit Git pin and copy locally with SHA-256 receipts; no source text is transmitted. Legacy repository helpers copy current working-tree files and do not uniformly enforce Git pins, tracked membership or hash receipts. Native package builds and downloads have separate network, execution and storage flows described in their installation documentation.
dataflow.method: Caller supplies authorized context; existing promise and boundaries govern output.
dataflow.native_runtime: Provider/network/storage flows are owned by native interfaces and host authorization; these files do not enable them.

source_policy.revision: The shared canonical portable installer (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/) requires an explicit full 40-character Git commit and never infers latest. This guarantee does not apply uniformly to legacy or native installers; the legacy repository helper is an operator-controlled working-tree copy without Git-pin, tracked-membership or SHA-256 receipt enforcement.
source_policy.repository_rename: Public identity may change; skill folder, imports, entrypoints, tool IDs and schemas remain stable.
source_policy.research: .research/market remains local and ignored; AGENTS governs refresh.

film.heading: Find the seam. Then build the slice.
film.blurb: In 70 seconds, Tock the metronome copies the conductor into the lobby to show progress, so two loops keep time and Cancel stops only the copy. Build with Amplifier finds the right seam in the host you installed, hangs a hook so the lobby only listens, and proves the slice: success, bad input, cancel and cleanup. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: The app and its music importer are a fictional example. The film shows how the skill behaves; it does not report results.

shared_portable.applies_when: portable_method is declared; otherwise describe native interfaces without executing installation
guarantees: Tracked portable source membership and source-byte checks

legacy_repository.documentation: Existing install_commands and repository installation documentation, where provided.
legacy_repository.source_policy: Operator-controlled current working-tree copy. It can include untracked files and can operate outside a Git checkout; no uniform Git pin or SHA-256 transaction receipt is enforced.
legacy_repository.permissions: Review the specific command and destination; shared-installer transaction and permission guarantees do not describe this route.

native.documentation: interfaces.native, runtime_install_commands and project installation documentation, where provided.
native.source_policy: Native packaging, host composition and download routes retain their own version and provenance rules; shared portable receipt guarantees do not automatically apply.
native.permissions: Package builds may execute build tools; dependency or artifact downloads may use the network. Review the documented command, dependencies, destination and runtime authorization separately.
